objective_for_doctor:
Age: 52
Sex: Male
Chief Complaint: I have right side of the chest pain, left side of the chest pain, and right posterior chest wall pain

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I have severe chest pain on both sides—sharp, like a knife-stab feeling—and pain in the right back side of my chest. I also feel very short of breath, and I have left calf swelling; I even lost consciousness.
[ASK] Do you have **wheezing or a history of asthma/COPD with shortness of breath that improves after bronchodilator**?
No, I don’t have wheezing, and I don’t have a history of asthma or COPD. My shortness of breath doesn’t feel like it improves after any inhaler or bronchodilator.
[ASK] Do you have chest pain or pressure that is worse with exertion or does not go away at rest (lasting >10 minutes)?

The chest pain is very sharp and stabbing, and it doesn’t really go away. I can’t say it gets worse specifically with exertion, but it’s been persistent and severe even at rest, lasting more than 10 minutes.
[ASK] Do you have shortness of breath that is sudden or out of proportion to exertion (especially with pleuritic chest pain)?
Yes—my shortness of breath feels sudden and is out of proportion to what I’m doing. It also comes with pleuritic chest pain, like it hurts more when I breathe in.
[ASK] Are you currently experiencing chest pain or pressure that is worse with exertion and/or does not go away with rest?
Yes. I’m still having the chest pain now. It’s sharp and stabbing and doesn’t really go away even when I’m resting.
